text:
Marathon Petroleum closed down 0.7% today after releasing its quarterly earnings report this morning. The stock has fallen 10% over two weeks despite relatively stable oil prices (US crude around $103/barrel), suggesting the market's reaction to the company's numbers and forward guidance was disappointing—particularly given the CNBC warning from four days ago that Big Oil earnings guidance, not just past results, would be what investors focus on most.

The timing matters: a leadership change was announced alongside the earnings, which can add uncertainty even when underlying business conditions look reasonable. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with ample crude supply, so operational challenges don't appear to be the driver here—this looks more like a earnings-expectations or guidance issue that shifted investor sentiment on the stock.
